key_insight: A label-free PINN with incremental strength reduction can reproduce slope failure factors of safety and weak-zone mechanisms for spatially variable c-phi slopes, and a neural operator can then extrapolate these results to millions of random fields quickly.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster reliability assessment of heterogeneous slopes without direct finite-element solves for every realization, supporting probabilistic geotechnical design and screening.
method: Physics-informed neural network trained with a virtual-work loss on the finite-element mesh
Non-associated Mohr-Coulomb plasticity with incremental strength reduction for random c-phi fields
Neural operator trained on PINN-generated solutions to predict factor of safety, displacement path, and failure mode
evidence_signal: On 52 random fields, the PINN matched Abaqus factor of safety within 2-3% RMS and identified the same weak zones, while Monte Carlo, FORM, importance sampling, and the operator agreed on failure probabilities down to 1e-3.
watch_item: The reported probabilities are sensitive to small factor-of-safety scatter and are tied to one mesh, while the plastic strain band is under-resolved.
paper_title: Label-free physics-informed strength reduction and a neural operator for the reliability of spatially variable slopes
